title: Polyglot evaluation prompt set — CJK, RTL, translation & locale regression
body:
Purpose:
This working doc collects a curated prompt set and regression checklist for onboarding new models to Redwood’s hosted and dedicated inference surfaces. Focus: CJK (Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean), RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian/Farsi), translation-quality edge cases, and locale formatting (dates, numbers, currencies, plurals, bidi).

Scope and goals:
- Provide reproducible prompt/response pairs where possible so automatic regressions can run (sacréBLEU/chrF + human checklist).
- Surface common failure modes for production prompts: tokenization divergence, punctuation normalization, bidi/mirrored punctuation, numeral systems, calendar/locales, honorifics, and short-form vs long-form translation consistency.
- Establish quick accept/reject thresholds per language for onboarding (suggested thresholds below).

How this artifact is used:
- Roundtrip tests in the onboarding pipeline (source -> model -> target).
- Human review items are flagged for ambiguous or context-dependent translations.
- Regression harness compares model output to stored references; failing cases create tickets with model, prompt, and diff.

Test categories and representative prompts (short sampling):
1) CJK: lexical ambiguity and punctuation
- zh-CN (Simplified): "我昨天去银行。"  // ambiguous: riverbank vs financial bank; expect clarifying translation or consistent policy (prefer financial in finance prompts).
- zh-TW (Traditional): "他把檔案存在桌面。"  // test file-system vocabulary and Traditional characters.
- ja-JP: "明日、研修がありますか？" // honorifics and polite forms; ensure masu/te forms where appropriate.
- ko-KR: "회의는 오후 3시로 변경되었습니다." // time formatting and spacing rules.
Notes: include baseline reference translations and allow multiple acceptable variants; mark as human-verified if multiple variants accepted.

2) RTL: bidi and punctuation quirks
- ar (Modern Standard Arabic): "هل تريد نقل الملف إلى الدليل الرئيسي؟" // Arabic punctuation, trailing punctuation direction, numeral use (Arabic-Indic vs European digits).
- he (Hebrew): "המסמך נשמר בתיקיה בשם Reports." // directionality with embedded Latin 'Reports'.
- fa (Farsi): "تاریخ ملاقات: ۱۴۰۲/۱۲/۲۰" // Persian calendar vs Gregorian; numeric system.
Notes: test mixed LTR/RTL runs: e.g., English pathnames inside Arabic/Hebrew. Expect preserved Latin strings and proper bidi markers or U+202A/U+202B only when necessary.

3) Translation quality and ambiguity edge cases
- Ambiguous pronouns: EN source: "Alex told Jordan that they would join." // Ensure model resolves or marks ambiguous pronoun appropriately; for translations into gendered languages expect either neutral phrasing or human review.
- Idioms and cultural localization: EN: "kick the bucket" -> should be localized, not literal.
- Named entities: maintain entity form vs localized names (decide per-domain).

4) Locale formatting tests (dates, numbers, currencies, lists, pluralization)
- Date formats: EN->ja: "03/04/2026" -> ambiguous; tests for expected target (year-first in JP: 2026年3月4日).
- Currency: "$1,234.56" -> zh-CN should be converted to ￥1,234.56 or remain $ depending on policy; specify per-test expected behavior.
- Decimal separators: "1,234.56" vs "1.234,56" tests for de/ru locales.
- Percent and spacing rules: French non-breaking space before % in fr-FR; verify in RTL that percent sign placement follows locale.

Reference prompts and expected outputs (examples):
- Test ID: CJK-001
  Source (zh-CN): "请把报告上传到共享盘，然后通知李经理。"
  Expected (en baseline): "Please upload the report to the shared drive and then notify Manager Li."
  Notes: preserve proper nouns and honorifics; '经理' -> 'Manager' vs 'Mr./Ms.' configurable by domain.

- Test ID: RTL-003
  Source (ar): "ملف التثبيت في C:\Program Files\App"
  Expected (en baseline): "The install file is in C:\Program Files\App"
  Notes: path must remain LTR; test for correct embedding and no inserted bidi markers in plain text outputs.

Scoring and acceptance criteria:
- Automatic metrics: sacréBLEU >= language-specific threshold OR chrF >= threshold. Suggested starting thresholds (conservative for onboarding):
  - CJK (ZH/JA/KO): chrF >= 0.40 or BLEU >= 20 (short strings may not hit BLEU);
  - RTL (AR/HE/FA): chrF >= 0.38 or BLEU >= 18;
  - High-variance / idioms: require human verification even if metric passes.
- Human review scale (1-5): 1=incorrect, 3=adequate, 5=perfect production-ready. For onboarding, median human score >= 4 required for launch.
- Blocking failures: wrong numeric/date/currency conversion, breaking LTR/RTL embedding, tokenization that strips diacritics in Arabic/Hebrew in a way that changes meaning.

Regression harness notes:
- Store reference outputs per model version in the onboarding repo (git LFS for large sets).
- Run bilingual automatic scoring for new model candidate vs reference. If automatic metric drop > 10% relative to baseline, create a regression alert.
- Flag flaky tests: very short strings or very long context produce unstable metrics; tag these for human review and possible exclusion from strict gating.

Operational checklist for onboarding:
- [ ] Populate language-specific prefix instructions (preserve Latin substrings, date/currency policy).
- [ ] Run automatic metrics job (CI) and collect diffs for failing cases.
- [ ] Assign human reviewers for flagged ambiguous/idiomatic cases (eng-applied-ml + native speaker reviewer).
- [ ] Validate locale formatting tests in target deployment locales (hosted vs dedicated may have region-specific defaults).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Policy decision: numeric system normalization (Arabic-Indic digits vs European digits) — should this follow user locale or source text? (Owner: Lina)
- Do we canonicalize honorifics across languages (Manager Li -> Li Manager vs Mr. Li)? Need product guidance for enterprise docs. (Owner: Mateo)
- Short-string scoring: metrics are noisy under 10 tokens — need a curated long-form set vs short sanity checks. (Owner: Kenji)

Next steps / timeline:
- 2026-02-15: finalize test list for onboarding sprint 1 (owner Emily).
- 2026-02-22: CI integration PR to run sacreBLEU/chrF daily on candidate builds (linked PR in GitHub).
- 2026-03-05: human review pass for initial failures; update references where multiple variants accepted.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working doc. Please comment inline on ambiguous expected outputs and add alternative accepted translations under the test ID using the format 'ALT:'.
- For any new language add a short section with locale rules and an initial 20 test cases (10 deterministic, 10 ambiguous).

Appendix: sample ambiguous prompts for human review (quick list)
- EN -> ja: "They left the meeting early because of him."
- EN -> ar: "The protest was peaceful, but it turned violent later."
- zh -> en: "她把杯子放在桌子上，走了。" (tense/aspect and subject reference)

Contact: Emily Chen (eng-applied-ml) — add collaborators for native review cycles.

Revision history:
- 2026-02-10: created; initial seed prompts and scoring suggestions.
- 2026-03-12: expanded RTL tests, added locale-formatting checklist and CI notes.
